Compute composite score for cell groups

compute_composite_score.Rd

Computes a composite score by performing Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) between the deconvolution features of a cell group and the score of its TF module (module eigengene). The score is the weighted sum of the (scaled) features of the cell group, with the weights of the first canonical component: the combination of the features that correlates most with the TF module score (with a single module score, this is the linear regression of the module score on the features, up to a scaling factor). As the sign of CCA weights is arbitrary, the score is oriented so that it is aligned with the TF module: a positive score means that the sample is on the active side of the module for that cell group. The score therefore increases with the features of the cell group when they are positively related to the module, and decreases with them when they are negatively related.

Usage

compute_composite_score(cell_group, module, network, batch = NULL)

Arguments

cell_group

A numeric matrix of cell deconvolution features for a cell group (samples x features), with sample names as row names. The module score of network is matched to these samples by name; every sample must be in the network.

module

Character. Name (color) of the TF module the cell group was built from; must match a column name of the module matrix in network exactly.

network

Output of compute.WTCNA() (single- or multi-cohort).

batch

Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the row order of cell_group. It is treated as categorical: the cell group features are z-scored within each cohort (mean 0, SD 1 per cohort; a feature constant in a cohort is 0 there) before the CCA. The module score is used as it is: compute.WTCNA() already scales it within each cohort.

Value

An unnamed list of two elements:

  • [[1]]: Numeric matrix (samples x 1) with the composite score, i.e. the scaled cell group features projected onto the first canonical component, oriented to be aligned with the TF module. With batch, it has mean 0 within each cohort.

  • [[2]]: Projection parameters used to score new samples: xcoef (canonical weights of the first component), train_means and train_sds (column means/SDs used for scaling). The sign of xcoef follows the orientation of the score. When batch correction was applied, only xcoef is returned: new samples are then z-scored on their own means and SDs, as each training cohort was.

Details

The CCA is reliable only when the number of features of the cell group is well below the number of samples. When it reaches the number of samples, the first canonical correlation is 1 whatever the data, the weights are not unique and the score is decided by numerical noise. Cell groups with many features and few samples (e.g. cross-validation folds) are the most affected.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled

#> Warning: Length of color vector was shorter than the number of clusters - color vector was recycled
#> Dendrogram plots saved to: Results/Dendrogram_color_clusters.pdf
#> 44 of 897 features were not assigned to any cluster by the tree cut and are not part of any cell group (pink: 2, yellow: 8, red: 2, blue: 6, brown: 4, turquoise: 12, black: 4, green: 6)
group <- names(cell_groups$Composition)[1]
module <- sub("^Dendrogram_(.*)_group_.*$", "\\1", group) # TF module of the cell group
features <- deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]][, cell_groups$Composition[[group]], drop = FALSE]
score <- compute_composite_score(features, module, network.tuto)
head(score[[1]])
